raw_case_text:
The patient is a 49-year-old male with a past medical history of mantle cell lymphoma treated with autologous stem cell transplant in 2017 and maintenance rituximab until July 2020. He was initially hospitalized for 2 days with COVID-19 pneumonia in November 2020. He had no prior history of pneumonia while on rituximab therapy. From November 2020 to March 2021, he was hospitalized four times for recurrent shortness of breath and fever, for which he was diagnosed with recurrent pneumonia based on his clinical symptoms and pulmonary infiltrates on chest imaging. The patient had an extensive infectious disease workup throughout this time, which was negative, including for recurrent COVID-19 infection. During each case, he was treated with antibiotics and steroids with improvement in symptoms, but his respiratory symptoms returned within a few days upon discontinuing steroids and antibiotics. The patient also reported daily fevers, chills, night sweats, decreased appetite, and a 35-pound weight loss over the past 4 months.
The patient presented to our facility in March 2021 with recurrent shortness of breath and fever of 102 F. A chest x-ray revealed multifocal pulmonary opacities concerning for cryptogenic organizing pneumonia or interstitial pneumonia (Figure 1). He also underwent computed tomography (CT) angiography which showed patchy bilateral lung infiltrates and interstitial thickening concerning for pneumonia with pulmonary edema (Figure 2). Infectious disease workup was negative, including gram stain, respiratory culture, fungal culture, AFB smear and culture, blastomycosis, histoplasmosis, pneumocystis, legionella, and aspergillus. The patient also underwent a bronchoscopy, bronchoalveolar lavage, and lung biopsy, which showed chronic inflammation but was negative for wall cultures and malignancy. Laboratories were significant for hypogammaglobulinemia: IgG 260 mg/dL, IgA 19 mg/dL, and IgM 7 mg/dL. The patient had several risk factors for hypogammaglobulinemia, including a history of immune suppression for hematopoietic stem cell transplant in 2017, maintenance rituximab until July 2020, and multiple short courses of glucocorticoids. The patient was managed with broad-spectrum antibiotics, a reduction in steroid dose, and administration of intravenous immunoglobulins (IVIG).
At his 1-month follow-up visit, the patient reported marked improvements in his symptoms. He stated he has continued to have some occasional cough and sinus drainage but denied any continued fevers, chills, or night sweats. He also reported improvement in shortness of breath with exertion.

subjective.chief_complaint: A 49-year-old male with mantle cell lymphoma in remission after autologous stem cell transplant and maintenance rituximab presented in March 2021 with a 4-month history of recurrent febrile pneumonia admissions, daily fevers (102 °F), chills, night sweats, anorexia, exertional dyspnea, and a 35-pound weight loss following a November 2020 COVID-19 hospitalization.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: Having undergone autologous stem cell transplantation in 2017 and maintenance rituximab through July 2020 for mantle cell lymphoma without prior pulmonary infections, the patient was hospitalized for 2 days in November 2020 with COVID-19 pneumonia. Between November 2020 and March 2021, he required four separate hospitalizations for recurrent shortness of breath, daily fevers, chills, night sweats, anorexia, a 35-pound weight loss, and migratory pulmonary infiltrates that transiently improved with empiric antibiotics and corticosteroids but relapsed within days of stopping therapy, culminating in his fifth presentation in March 2021 with dyspnea and a 102 °F fever.
subjective.past_medical_history: Mantle cell lymphoma status post autologous hematopoietic stem cell transplantation in 2017 and maintenance rituximab completed in July 2020; COVID-19 pneumonia in November 2020 followed by four hospitalizations for culture-negative relapsing pneumonia.
subjective.review_of_systems: Positive for recurrent shortness of breath, daily fevers (up to 102 °F), chills, night sweats, anorexia, and a 35-pound weight loss over 4 months.

objective.physical_examination: Febrile to 102 °F with shortness of breath on March 2021 presentation.
objective.routine_investigations: Immunoglobulin panel: Profound panhypogammaglobulinemia with serum IgG 260 mg/dL, IgA 19 mg/dL, and IgM 7 mg/dL. Comprehensive microbiological workup (across admissions): Repeatedly negative for SARS-CoV-2 reinfection, Gram stain, respiratory bacterial culture, fungal culture, AFB smear and culture, Blastomyces, Histoplasma, Pneumocystis jirovecii, Legionella, and Aspergillus. Chest radiograph: Multifocal pulmonary opacities.
objective.advanced_workup: CT chest angiography: Patchy bilateral lung infiltrates and interstitial thickening. Bronchoscopy with bronchoalveolar lavage (BAL) and transbronchial/lung biopsy: Chronic pulmonary inflammation with negative tissue/BAL cultures and no evidence of lymphoma relapse or malignancy.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation: Final diagnosis: Severe secondary panhypogammaglobulinemia (IgG 260 mg/dL, IgA 19 mg/dL, IgM 7 mg/dL; induced by prior autologous stem cell transplant, maintenance rituximab through July 2020, and repeated steroid courses) presenting as relapsing culture-negative organizing/interstitial pneumonia after November 2020 COVID-19 infection, with Pneumocystis jirovecii, fungal, mycobacterial, and malignant etiologies excluded by bronchoscopy and lung biopsy. Plan and clinical course: Managed with intravenous immunoglobulin (IVIG) replacement therapy, broad-spectrum antibiotics, and steroid tapering; at 1-month follow-up, his fevers, chills, night sweats, and exertional dyspnea had markedly resolved.
